title: The wall cleaner that became Play-Doh
hook: Play-Doh was invented to clean walls, not for play.
summary: Play-Doh began in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner, nearly died when coal heating faded, and was saved when a teacher gave it to children.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica / Wikipedia 'Play-Doh': created by Noah McVicker at Kutol Products, Cincinnati, as a wallpaper cleaner in the 1930s; sales fell as coal heating declined; sold as a toy in 1956.
Smithsonian / Strong National Museum of Play: Kay Zufall, a nursery school teacher and sister-in-law of Joseph McVicker, used it with children and suggested it as a modelling compound.

lines.text: Play-Doh was invented to clean walls, not for play.
In the nineteen thirties, a Cincinnati company sold it to wipe soot off wallpaper.

lines.text: But homes stopped burning coal, and sales dried up.
Then a nursery school teacher, Kay Zufall, tried it with her pupils.

lines.text: The children loved shaping it, so she told her brother-in-law.

lines.text: He dropped the cleaning idea and, in nineteen fifty-six, sold it as a toy.

lines.text: A dying wall cleaner became a toy children still use today.

post.caption:
Play-Doh started as a soot remover for wallpaper and was nearly forgotten.
What everyday thing do you think started as something else?
